conviction_note: The event is real but has almost no content: the FY-to-30-June-2026 statutory accounts of a producer whose June-quarter production, AISC, cash and bullion (US$364.3m), debt (US$130m) and the US$13.8m merger CGT settlement were all lodged on 30 July, and whose CEO restated guidance and cash at Mining Forum Americas on 28 September. PDI's prior statutory-accounts lodgements moved it +2.2% (2025-09-05), +1.5% (2026-05-13) and +5.0% on a day with other news (2026-02-23). Nothing found that the price does not already hold, so 0.
bar: PDI's own statement of 4 May 2026 that it would lodge an annual financial report for the 12 months to 30 June 2026 by 30 September 2026 (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260504/pdf/06z6rt69n9bnwq.pdf). filer_type_check: The baseline reads quarterly_report_only, but that is the classifier missing PDI's statutory accounts, not a missing print. The archive shows 'Full Year Statutory Accounts' on 2024-09-04 and 2025-09-05, 'Half Year Accounts' on 2026-02-23 and 'Consolidated Financial Statements 31 March 2026' on 2026-05-13 (PDI is also a TSX reporting issuer, so it files quarterly statements too). None of those headlines is an Appendix 4E. This event is a statutory annual financial report and not a 5B quarterly. So I hunted for anything in the FY26 accounts the quarterlies do not already show, meaning acquisition accounting for Robex, a Nampala (Mali) impairment, going concern or audit qualifications, and a capital return. I also checked what else could land inside the one-session window.
event_check: The company has publicly committed to the date. In its 4 May 2026 'Change of Financial Year End' announcement (ASX idsId 03090089, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260504/pdf/06z6rt69n9bnwq.pdf) PDI moves its year end from 30 June to 31 December and says it 'will lodge an annual financial report for the twelve-month period to 30 June 2026 by 30 September 2026'. The 2026 ASX archive (https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=PDI&timeframe=Y&year=2026) has no annual report yet: the latest items are dated 28/09/2026. That means 30 September is the statutory deadline and not a vendor guess. The CEO also flagged 'annual results' for quarter-end at Mining Forum Americas on 28 Sep (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/pdi-gold-at-mining-forum-americas-2026-low-costs-big-growth-93CH-4921061). One risk remains: a lodgement on the evening of 29 September would land before this window opens.
session_check: Not settled. The vendor says amc. PDI's own recent financial-statement lodgements were in session: Half Year Accounts at 3:54 pm on 23/02/2026 and the 31 March 2026 statements at 2:51 pm on 13/05/2026. The FY24 and FY25 statutory accounts came pre-open, at 8:24 am and 8:20 am. So an in-session lodgement on 30 September, with part of any reaction landing before the window's opening close, is at least as likely as amc. Source: the ASX archive pages for 2024, 2025 and 2026 (https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=PDI&timeframe=Y&year=2026). With nothing sized, this changes nothing.
positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short is 3.7046% as of 2026-09-23, up from 3.6556% on 2026-09-16 (+0.049pp), with a lag of 4 sessions. That is flat, neither building nor covering, and moderate rather than crowded. Nothing in it argues for or against a move, and it gives no reason to lean against the +1.49 priced lean, which is mostly the prior-weighted squeeze term. The +12.4% on 6.9m shares on 2026-09-18, with no PDI announcement that day, matches index-rebalance buying into the S&P DJI September effective date. The substantial-holder notices of 24 and 28 September fit that too, but I did not verify it and sized nothing on it.

outside_window.finding: Bankan exploitation permit. The CEO said on 28 Sep 2026 that the permit was expected 'imminently' after a presidential meeting, and that construction could start once the wet season ends. The application has been 'in the final stages' of review since mid-2025, and on 30 July 2026 it was still pending. Arrival timing is random and the market has been told repeatedly that it is coming. It is a large binary positive when it lands (about +5 to +12), but the chance it lands in this one session is small and the expectation is presumably priced across dates, so I did not rank it.
The Guinea domestic gold-refining decree's 90-day transition ends on 6 October 2026. The company says it expects no material impact.

September-quarter production update. The June-quarter one came on 8 July, so this one should arrive in early October, outside the window. On 28 Sep the CEO said Kiniero was on track to meet or beat the top of guidance at about 176koz, which is already public.
The updated Bankan DFS, which optimises the mill size and capex, is guided for December 2026.
